why: How a consultation ended, as a word. Both halves of this product have their own copy of this
catalogue — the server validates against it before writing anything, and the panel turns it into
the sentence a person reads and the choices a person is offered — and the two ship separately, so
a word added to one and not the other is a refusal nobody can explain from the other side.
Neither half owns this file. Each asserts its OWN catalogue against it, which is the shape
`NothingReadsAnotherProgramsSourceTests` requires: a suite that read the other program's source
to derive its expectation goes quiet on a reformat instead of going red.
`verdict` is the distinction the whole feature turns on. Three of these are somebody's statement
about whether the advice was any good. `lapsed` is the server's own statement that the clock ran
out, which is a fact about time — so it is not a verdict, it may be replaced by one, and no
caller and no person may write it.

outcomes.label: Solved
outcomes.detail: the advice was verified and it worked

outcomes.label: Not solved
outcomes.detail: it was verified and it did not

outcomes.label: Abandoned
outcomes.detail: nobody is going to act on it
the budget ran out or it sat idle — written by the server and by nobody else

sources.detail: the AI that opened the consultation, through the `close_consult` tool
a human, through the panel's own one-shot `--close-consult` door
nobody said anything and the clock ran out; only ever beside `lapsed`
